reference: GNU Git (pack-objects, verify-pack, cat-file, unpack-objects) provides the independent object and pack oracle; GNU find is used for directory enumeration. The fixed pack/index fixture is encoded independently in Python from the published Git pack v2 and index v2 layouts using SHA-1, zlib, CRC-32, and big-endian fields. The create-self-roundtrip-result case compares payload recovery only: the candidate verifies/reads its own output, so this case does not establish independent Git readability of candidate packs.
coverage: Bash builtin discovery and help metadata contract.
Binary blob read from an independently encoded pack/index, including an embedded NUL byte.
Index object enumeration and pack-file listing.
Valid pack/index checksum and CRC verification, plus invalid index rejection.
Unpack into a fresh loose-object database and read back the recovered bytes.
Candidate pack/index creation, self-verification and self-readback, comparing recovered payload bytes with Git's corresponding result; external readability is unqualified.
exclusions: Only one blob object is covered; commit, tree, and tag objects, multi-object sorting/fanout, OFS_DELTA and REF_DELTA chains, and malformed pack bodies are not exercised.
A >2 GiB pack offset is deferred because the mandatory runner file and memory limits cannot hold a valid pack that reaches the 64-bit index-offset path.
No network transport or system operation is part of the pack builtin scope tested here.

Candidate-created packs/indexes are verified and read only by the candidate implementation; create-self-roundtrip-result compares payload recovery, not independent pack-format conformance. External Git readability of candidate output remains unqualified.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports pack as a builtin and exposes its documented help entry.
cases.script:
if [ "$(type -t pack)" = builtin ]; then
  help pack >/dev/null
  printf 'builtin with help\n'
else
  printf 'pack metadata missing\n'
fi

cases.purpose: Read a NUL-containing blob from a fixed pack and v2 index independently encoded from the published Git formats; compare with Git reading the same packed object. Filesystem comparison is disabled because GNU git init leaves repository template metadata absent from the hand-built candidate fixture; stdout and status still compare.
cases.script:
sha=2fd9480f8ce3ca984096feb2709e28824b090cec
pack_file=packrepo/.git/objects/pack/fixture.pack
idx_file=packrepo/.git/objects/pack/fixture.idx
if [ "$(type -t pack)" = builtin ]; then
  mkdir -p packrepo/.git/objects/pack
  printf '[core]\nrepositoryformatversion = 0\nbare = true\n' > packrepo/.git/config
  printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > packrepo/.git/HEAD
else
  mkdir -p packrepo
  git init -q --bare packrepo/.git
fi
printf '%b' '\x50\x41\x43\x4b\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x00\x00\x01\xbb\x01\x78\x9c\x2b\x48\x2c\xca\x2c\xa9\x54\x48\xcb\xac\x28\x29\x2d\x4a\x65\x28\xcf\x2c\xc9\x50\x48\xca\xcc\x4b\x2c\xaa\xe4\x02\x00\x94\x03\x0a\x2c\xb8\x39\xcc\x98\x1a\x04\x34\xc9\x1f\x21\x99\xd8\x77\xd4\x12\xa9\x60\xa6\xe0\x7d' > "$pack_file"
{
  printf '%b' '\xfftOc\x00\x00\x00\x02'
  for ((i=0; i<256; i++)); do
    if (( i < 47 )); then
      printf '%b' '\x00\x00\x00\x00'
    else
      printf '%b' '\x00\x00\x00\x01'
    fi
  done
  printf '%b' '\x2f\xd9\x48\x0f\x8c\xe3\xca\x98\x40\x96\xfe\xb2\x70\x9e\x28\x82\x4b\x09\x0c\xec\xf6\x6d\xd5\xf6\x00\x00\x00\x0c\xb8\x39\xcc\x98\x1a\x04\x34\xc9\x1f\x21\x99\xd8\x77\xd4\x12\xa9\x60\xa6\xe0\x7d\x15\xc2\x88\x57\x30\xee\x2b\x10\x31\x43\xee\x5b\x80\x1d\x9d\xb5\x39\xf1\xe9\xc8'

  pack cat "$pack_file" "$idx_file" "$sha"

fi

cases.purpose: Compare decoded round-trip results with the independently known blob payload and Git's corresponding round trip: create a pack/index from a fixed loose blob, run the same implementation's index verifier, remove the loose copy, and read its pack. This does not independently validate the candidate pack or prove external Git readability. Filesystem comparison is disabled because Git initialization creates unrelated template metadata and pack encodings need not be byte-identical; decoded bytes and status still compare.
cases.script:
sha=2fd9480f8ce3ca984096feb2709e28824b090cec
loose_path=source/.git/objects/2f/d9480f8ce3ca984096feb2709e28824b090cec
if [ "$(type -t pack)" = builtin ]; then
  mkdir -p source/.git/objects/2f source/.git/objects/pack
  printf '[core]\nrepositoryformatversion = 0\nbare = true\n' > source/.git/config
  printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > source/.git/HEAD
else
  mkdir -p source
  git init -q --bare source/.git
fi
mkdir -p source/.git/objects/2f
printf '%b' '\x78\x9c\x4b\xca\xc9\x4f\x52\x30\x32\x67\x28\x48\x2c\xca\x2c\xa9\x54\x48\xcb\xac\x28\x29\x2d\x4a\x65\x28\xcf\x2c\xc9\x50\x48\xca\xcc\x4b\x2c\xaa\xe4\x02\x00\xda\x4f\x0c\x54' > "$loose_path"
pack_path=source/.git/objects/pack/candidate.pack
idx_path=source/.git/objects/pack/candidate.idx
if [ "$(type -t pack)" = builtin ]; then
  pack create "$pack_path" --idx "$idx_path" -r source "$sha" >/dev/null
  pack verify-idx "$idx_path" "$pack_path"
  rm "$loose_path"
  pack cat "$pack_path" "$idx_path" "$sha"
  rm "$pack_path" "$idx_path"
else
  pack_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$sha" | git --git-dir=source/.git pack-objects --window=0 --depth=0 source/.git/objects/pack/reference)
  git verify-pack -v "source/.git/objects/pack/reference-$pack_id.idx" >/dev/null
  rm "$loose_path"
  git --git-dir=source/.git cat-file blob "$sha"
  rm "source/.git/objects/pack/reference-$pack_id.pack" "source/.git/objects/pack/reference-$pack_id.idx"
fi

cases.purpose: Exercise pack cat through an index v2 64-bit offset entry above the 32-bit offset range.
cases.reason: The runner limits individual files to 8 MiB and process memory to 768 MiB, while pack cat slurps the complete pack into memory. A valid object after offset 0x80000000 cannot be represented within those limits. A future disposable VM should use a sparse pack constructor or a bounded seek/read mock, produce an index v2 overflow table that Git verify-pack accepts, and compare the object bytes and status with git cat-file. This case does not execute.
